title: Operational debt repayment playbook for platform services
author: Evelyn Chen
content:
Purpose

This playbook defines a standardized lifecycle for identifying, prioritizing, scheduling, and verifying repayment of operational debt across Redwood's platform services. It is aimed at platform owners, operators, product partners, and SREs responsible for keeping service reliability, cost, and operational complexity within acceptable bounds.

Scope

- Applies to platform subsystems: routing, batching, KV prefix cache, scheduling, GPU pool plumbing, telemetry ingestion, and rollout orchestration.
- Covers technical debt (code & design), process debt (runbooks, oncall docs), and cost debt (inefficient patterns causing sustained over-spend).

Definitions

- Operational debt: Any backlog item that reduces reliability, increases cost, or materially slows down operator and developer productivity and which has been deferred.
- Repayment lifecycle: Discover -> Assess -> Prioritize -> Plan -> Implement -> Verify -> Close.

Scoring and prioritization rubric (use per-candidate)

Each candidate is scored 0-5 on the following dimensions and multiplied by the weight to get a total debt priority score. Use the provided spreadsheet template for batch scoring.

| Dimension                | Weight | 0 (none) | 3 (moderate) | 5 (critical) |
|-------------------------|--------|----------|--------------|--------------|
| Customer impact (user-visible failures, SLO burn) | 4 | negligible | occasional SLO noise | frequent SLO breaches / outages |
| Operator burden (pages, toil, manual steps)       | 3 | none | some repetitive work | frequent manual interventions required |
| Cost impact (monthly $)                          | 2 | unmeasurable | moderate recurring cost | significant recurring cost (> $Xk/month) |
| Risk (security/regulatory/availability)         | 3 | minimal | medium | high / compliance exposure |
| Time-to-fix (estimated dev-days)                | -1 | trivial | moderate | large (increases lead time) |
| Cross-service coupling                            | 1 | low | medium | high |

Scoring example: total = sum(weight*score) where score is 0..5 normalized. Use the ticket template fields for captured scores.

Repayment lifecycle: steps and responsibilities

1) Discover (owner: service team + platform triage board)
   - Sources: oncall retros, incident postmortems, cost dashboards, tech review sessions, SEV reports, third-party audit findings.
   - Create a "debt-candidate" ticket using the template: summary, impact scores, owner, tentative timeline, rollback plan.

2) Assess (owner: service owner + SRE reviewer)
   - Run the scoring rubric. Capture SLO delta if fixed. Estimate dev-days and required test/QA time.
   - Attach a minimal architecture diagram and dependency list.

3) Prioritize (owner: platform product council / triage board)
   - Weekly triage: rank candidates by priority score and cost-of-delay. Ensure a mix of short-risk quick wins and high-impact projects.
   - Reserve at least 10% of platform sprint capacity for debt repayment across teams (see budget below).

4) Plan (owner: service owner)
   - Break the candidate into incremental milestones with measurable acceptance criteria and verification tests.
   - Define a canary plan and rollback criteria if the change touches runtime or scheduling logic.

5) Implement (owner: assigned engineers)
   - Follow standard branch/PR rules, include performance regressions bench results in PR description.
   - Add or update runbook steps and add instrumentation where needed.

6) Verify (owner: SRE + QA)
   - Run the pre-defined verification checklist (see Checklist subsection). Monitor baseline SLOs and cost metrics for 2 full burn-in windows or 14 days, whichever is longer.

7) Close (owner: service owner)
   - Merge changes, update debt ticket to "closed", and publish a 1-page summary in the team Retro with metrics showing impact.

Verification checklist (minimum)

- Unit and integration tests: green
- Benchmark: no >5% latency regression on 95th percentile unless explicitly traded off and documented
- Cost delta measured and under planned threshold (if applicable)
- Observable: new or updated dashboards for the feature are created and linked to the ticket
- Runbook: oncall playbook modified and validated by a secondary reviewer
- Rollout: canary policy defined (e.g., 5% RR for 6 hours -> 25% for 24 hours -> full)

Dashboard and alerting guidance

Mandatory dashboards (per service)
- Debt backlog dashboard: total open debt tickets, average priority score, mean age (days) of open items.
- Repayment velocity: closed debt items / sprint (rolling 4-week).
- Cost hotspots: services with top percentile of cost delta.
- Regression detector: post-deploy spike in SLO burn or error rates.

Suggested alert rules
- debt.backlog_count > 50 -> notify platform-triage@redwood (P3).
- repayment_velocity < 1 per team per month AND average priority > 60 -> notify eng-leads for remediation.
- debt.ticket_stalled > 30 days with owner assigned -> ping owner and secondary contact.

Budget and sprint allocation policy

- Target: at least 10% of engineering capacity across platform teams must be allocated to operational debt repayment each sprint. This can come from dedicated sprint time or "opt-in" days.
- Budgeted hours: each service should plan repayment in quarterly roadmaps and include expected dev-days in capacity planning.

Ticket and template conventions (always use)

- Label: debt-candidate, debt-priority-[score], service-[name].
- Fields to capture: Technical owner, Secondary owner, Score breakdown, Estimated dev-days, Expected SLO improvement, Rollout plan, Backout plan, Linked dashboards.

Example CLI & API snippets

- Create standardized ticket skeleton via our ticket-generator CLI:

  rwd-ticket create --template debt-candidate --service routing --owner @sally --summary "Fix KV cache hot-shard eviction causing 503s" --estimate 12d

- Query backlog from platform dashboard API:

  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $RWD_DASH" https://telemetry.internal/api/debt/backlog | jq .

Ownership matrix template (copy into ticket)

| Service | Primary owner | Secondary owner | SLO impacted | Typical repayment window |
|---------|---------------|-----------------|--------------|-------------------------|
| routing | @sally       | @marco          | request_p95 < 120ms | 1-3 sprints |
| kv-prefix-cache | @devin | @ravi         | cache_hit_ratio > 0.85 | 2-6 sprints |

Runbook for a high-risk repayment (example)

- Preconditions: feature branch merged to canary, canary infra available, templates updated.
- Rollout steps:
  1. Open change window (announce on #platform-ops).
  2. Deploy to canary subset (5% tenant weight).
  3. Monitor the following dashboards continuously for 6 hours: SLO burn, error rates, CPU/GPU utilization, token-cost-per-request.
  4. If any metric crosses the defined canary thresholds (see table), immediately rollback to previous version and file an incident.
  5. If canary stable, expand to 25% for 24 hours, continue monitoring.
  6. Full rollout with 1-hour post-check and final retrospective entry.

Canary thresholds (example)

| Metric | Threshold | Action |
|--------|-----------|--------|
| SLO 95th latency | > baseline * 1.15 | Rollback and investigate |
| Error rate | > baseline + 0.5% absolute | Rollback |
| Cost per token | > planned + 10% | Hold expansion, triage cost |

Reporting and KPIs

- Quarterly debt report (owner: platform product): backlog size, average priority score, repayment velocity, top 10 closed items with impact metrics.
- Goal: reduce high-priority backlog (>75 score) by 30% quarter-over-quarter.
- Metric definitions: replication in the dashboard template; use "debt_metric_v1" telemetry tag for all debt-related events.

Retro guidance after repayment completion

- Post-completion 15-minute sync with SRE and product to validate assumptions.
- Publish a 1-paragraph summary with: what changed, measurable impact, lessons learned, and follow-ups. Add to quarterly retro thread.

Common failure modes and mitigations

- Failure: Repayment introduces performance regression. Mitigation: block rollout until additional benchmarking and revert to canary.
- Failure: Debt ticket stalls. Mitigation: auto-escalate after 30 days to engineering lead and product sponsor.
- Failure: No measurable benefit post-closure. Mitigation: reopen ticket, add root-cause subtask to identify measurement gaps.
